task_cmo.answer: Brief Builder turns scattered client documents into a sourced Greek and English brief, highlighting disagreements and questions. For the agency, it aims to reduce preparation work; for me, it makes disputed commitments and missing answers easier to spot before creative work begins. This synthetic run passed 17 defined checks, preserved evidence and exposed three conflicts. It demonstrated a controlled drafting process, not proven savings or reliable everyday performance: the creative drafts still introduced errors. People confirm the facts, resolve disagreements, sign off and judge creative ideas. Nothing creative was delivered. I would support the conditional pilot to measure usefulness, review effort and actual costs.
missing: No essential information was missing for this explanation. Actual savings, operating costs and everyday reliability remain unproven, as the sheets acknowledge.
confusions: “a schema-validated edit in v1” — I cannot tell what practical task the account lead must perform or whether technical help is needed.
“question precision >80%, draft survival >70%” — these pilot success measures are not explained on the visible sheet.

“the two garbled terms were flagged, never repaired” followed by “the finished documents print the glossary term” — I had to infer that the original transcript stays unchanged while the draft uses the proposed term.
fixes: Replace “a schema-validated edit in v1” with “in this version, the account lead must edit the underlying brief file; the review page only displays the decisions”.
Replace “question precision >80%, draft survival >70%” with “over 80% of flagged questions judged relevant by the lead; over 70% of draft text retained without edits”.

Replace “the two garbled terms were flagged, never repaired” with “the original transcript was preserved; two garbled terms were flagged, and the drafts used the proposed glossary terms with citations”.
Replace “Re-baseline the changed routing before week 1.” with “Measure time and usage again before week 1 because the AI reading process has changed.”

task_cfo.answer: Stage-one tokens: Haiku 4.5=533,641; Sonnet 5=165,820+285,359=451,179; total=984,820. Creative adds 86,441 Sonnet and 63,473 Opus 4.8: total=1,134,734. Monthly: 984,820×15=14,772,300; one creative draft gives 15,724,395–16,068,915. Returned hours: [120−(20 assembling+30 reviewing)]×(15×12)/60=210/year; ×€19–20=€3,990–4,200 gross. Baseline, volume, rate and target attention are assumptions, not demonstrated savings. Approve four weeks: two leads, six retrospective projects, S0–S1, agency workspace, creative shadow. Before week 1, operator remeasures routing; management/operator validate subscription capacity/terms. Week-4 live use depends on retrospective targets: precision >80%, survival >70%, review <30 minutes, Greek quality and adoption. Exact release conditions and spending authority remain unclear.
missing: Pilot budget, spending ceiling, implementation/support effort and subscription cost; net benefit cannot be calculated.
A Greek-quality pass threshold and a clear distinction between week-4 release criteria and month-2 adoption targets.
An unequivocal mandatory stop rule and explicit approval gate for month-2 default rollout.
Measured review time and validation of the 50-minute attention target; the graded review was not timed.
confusions: “Stop rule, recommended: if weeks 2–3 miss the targets, week 4 does not go live.” Is this binding or merely proposed?
“Greek naturalness rated 1–5 with EL/EN edit comparison” gives a measurement method but no passing score.
“at least 3 further leads request onboarding in month 2” cannot determine whether week 4 may go live.

“Approve the four-week pilot: usage is measured in tokens, the cost of running it is not yet, and week 1 settles both.” Capacity and routing are elsewhere required before week 1, while no cost-estimation owner or approval ceiling is specified.
fixes: Change “Pilot effort and operating costs are still to be estimated.” to specify an estimation owner, deadline, spending ceiling and financial approval gate.
Change “Stop rule, recommended:” to state explicitly whether the rule is mandatory, and name the week-4 release decision owner.
Change “Greek naturalness rated 1–5 with EL/EN edit comparison” to include a passing threshold; separate week-4 criteria from month-2 adoption measures.
Change “from month 2 new projects start from a draft by default” to specify whether rollout requires a successful pilot and separate sponsor approval.

task_creative.answer: (a) Evidence: signed audience 25–40 urban professionals; launch 15 September 2026; production budget “in the eighties,” excluding media, without confirmed units or total; zero-sugar permission, brand constraints and requested video/key visuals. (b) Hypothesis: proposition, audience psychology, tone, reasons to believe and illustrative artwork; packaging remains undefined. (c) Strike “Greek-made,” €80–85k and the dance retraction; judge guilt wording against the health-claim ban. Choose A/B/neither, resolve six blockers—ingredients, video details, visual uses, TikTok-first scope, KPIs, milestones—and record creative approval. Creative remains evaluation-only in this version. (d) Specs are provisional traffic-table lookups: the gate guarantees token membership, not deliverable suitability, platform currency, layout safety or production readiness; traffic must confirm.
confusions: “Signed as the account lead’s was: in the run, by a named person, due before week 4 goes live.” This mixes a future creative approval with the completed account sign-off and leaves the scope of week-4 live use unclear.
“Feel: confident, refreshed, quietly proud it’s Greek” repeats an origin-adjacent suggestion beside the explicit rejection of “Greek-made”; its intended boundary is unclear.
fixes: Replace “Signed as the account lead’s was: in the run, by a named person, due before week 4 goes live.” with “Creative approval is pending: record the named lead’s choice and corrections. Week-4 client-brief use does not authorize creative delivery; creative stays in shadow in v1.”
Replace “quietly proud it’s Greek” with “quietly premium”; retain Greek identity or origin language only after confirming its factual basis.

Replace “The creative drafts stayed inside the signed-off facts and the spec table, except three things to strike and one call for the creative lead.” with “The drafts combine signed-off evidence with creative hypotheses. Three errors require correction, one claim needs judgement, and six open items still block production.”

task_engineer.answer: This synthetic run passed 17 checks; that proves fixture coverage, not general correctness. Code enforces readiness, schemas, exact anchors, glossary, sensitivity, sign-off and spec-token checks; it groups conflict candidates. Models classify, flag garbles, extract, verify, recognise contradictions, synthesise, render and draft creative. Failed extraction/synthesis/render gates allow one repair, then stop. Humans record resolutions and signoff in brief.json; brief_review.html displays them, toggles languages and copies questions, but does not save decisions or sign. Checks cannot establish semantic support, natural Greek, complete questions or appropriate spec rows; creative errors remain review work. Creative stays shadow-only. Before week 1, the operator must rerun usage/time measurements under Sonnet extraction plus verifier; management/operator must validate subscription capacity and terms.
confusions: “every line carrying its citation” sounds broader than the later limitation to “this run’s rendered claim lines”.
“every fact cites a brief entry” initially sounds like factual validation, despite the unsupported creative claims identified on the same sheet.
fixes: Replace “every line carrying its citation” with “this run’s claim lines carrying source tags; tags do not establish semantic support”.
Replace “every fact cites a brief entry” with “factual claims carry brief-entry tags, but unsupported claims can still pass into the draft”.
Replace “a schema-validated edit in v1” with “a schema-validated edit to brief.json in v1; the review page does not save resolutions or signatures”.
